title: Fidelity Orchestrator — telemetry contract and runbook
author: Marin Patel
content:
SUMMARY
-------
This document defines the Fidelity Orchestrator: a small, horizontally scalable control plane that uses live telemetry to decide kernel selection, execution fidelity, and degradation policies for inference requests. It contains the architecture overview, required telemetry contract (metrics/events), a deterministic decision flow, operational runbook for incidents, rollout checklists, and example policy snippets. The goal is predictable SLO adherence (latency/cost/quality) while enabling safe, measurable degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

AUDIENCE
--------
- Runtime engineers (owners, oncall)
- Kernel/scheduler team
- SRE and Observability
- Product owners for latency/cost tradeoffs

PROBLEM STATEMENT
-----------------
The runtime must route requests to optimal kernel variants and execution fidelities (full precision / quantized / reduced context / cached) without violating SLOs. Decisions must be based on standardized telemetry so they are auditable, testable, and reversible. Historically we saw oscillation when metrics lacked determinism and when fallback policies were underspecified.

COMPONENTS
----------
- fidelity-orchestrator (service name): stateless control plane exposing a gRPC decision API (/v1/decide) and an HTTP health endpoint.
- telemetry-ingest: stream aggregator that normalizes kernel and queue metrics and writes to the telemetry stream used by the orchestrator.
- decision-cache: fast in-memory cache (per-node) to keep recent decision results for identical signatures (TTL 30s).
- policy-store: versioned policy repository (Git-backed) with JSON policy files and canary rollout capability.

ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW
---------------------
Flow (simplified):
1) Request arrives at request-router with attributes: model_id, route, token_budget, interactive_flag, tenant_tier, seq_len_estimate.
2) Router forwards request to serving-runtime and asks fidelity-orchestrator: decide(request_signature, current_node_telemetry).
3) Orchestrator evaluates the policy with the telemetry snapshot and returns kernel_hint, exec_fidelity, fallback_chain.
4) Serving runtime applies hint and continues; decision cached locally for matching signatures.

CONTRACT: REQUIRED METRICS & EVENTS
-----------------------------------
All producing services must emit the following keys (metric names are canonical):

- kernel_latency_p50, kernel_latency_p95, kernel_latency_p99 (ms) — per kernel variant, 10s sliding window
- kernel_qps (rps) — per kernel variant
- kvcache_hit_ratio — per model-shard, 1m window
- request_queue_depth — per node, per queue-class
- outstanding_tokens_per_session — gauge
- token_cost_estimate_per_model (nanos) — model-level estimate for cost accounting
- recently_throttled (bool/event) — indicates prior admission throttles in last 30s
- node_cpu_pct, node_gpu_mem_free_mb — node health indicators
- model_quality_regressions (event) — evaluation flag from Optimize that can block aggressive quantization

Telemetry delivery semantics:
- Aggregation window: 10s for kernel latencies, 1m for kvcache and qps.
- Max ingestion lag: 5s — orchestrator must tolerate up to 10s stale snapshots but should annotate decisions with snapshot_age.
- Cardinality: metrics must include labels: model_id, kernel_variant, zone, tenant_tier.

DECISION RULES (simplified)
---------------------------
1) If request.interactive_flag == true and token_budget >= baseline_min_tokens (default 16) then prefer low-latency kernels if kernel_latency_p99 < interactive_p99_target (default 150ms) AND node_gpu_mem_free_mb > eviction_threshold (default 800MB).
2) If kvcache_hit_ratio > 0.6 and a cached_execution_variant exists, prefer cached path to reduce per-token cost (tie-breaker: if kernel_qps < kernel_qps_limit).
3) If model_quality_regressions flagged within 24h for model_id, block all aggressive quantization and enforce exec_fidelity == full_precision until cleared.
4) If request is from enterprise tenant_tier and SLA_priority == high, enforce fallback_chain that includes at least 1 alternate region.
5) If node health indicates thermal or memory pressure (node_gpu_mem_free_mb < 400MB OR node_cpu_pct > 90%), select degraded_fidelity (reduce batch-size, smaller kernel, or quantized variant) and set degrade_reason tag.

POLICY EXPRESSIONS
------------------
Policies are stored in policy-store as JSON. Example (illustrative):

{
  "id": "policy/interactive-default/v1",
  "conditions": [
    {"name": "is_interactive", "expr": "request.interactive_flag == true"},
    {"name": "p99_ok", "expr": "telemetry.kernel_latency_p99 < 150"}
  ],
  "action": {"kernel_hint": "kernel-lowlatency-v2", "exec_fidelity": "balanced"},
  "fallback": ["kernel-lowlatency-v1","kernel-quantized-v3"]
}

(The orchestrator enforces a schema; policies that fail validation are rejected by the CI gate.)

TRACE & ANNOTATION CONTRACT
---------------------------
Each decision call must annotate tracing/decision provenance for debugging:
- decision_id (uuid)
- snapshot_age_ms
- telemetry_keys_used (list)
- policy_id
- score_explain (short text: why chosen)

OPERATIONAL SLOS
----------------
- decision_api_p99_latency < 30ms (measured at request-router to orchestrator round-trip)
- decision_service_uptime: 99.95% monthly
- decision_cache_hit_rate >= 40% for common interactive signatures

RUNBOOK: INCIDENTS & MITIGATION
--------------------------------
Detection (automated alerts):
- Alert A1: decision_api_p99_latency > 50ms for 5m (SEV-2)
- Alert A2: unexpected_jump_in_degradation_rate > 5% in 10m (SEV-1 when > 20% tenant-impact)
- Alert A3: policy-validation-failures during rollout > 1 per deploy (SEV-2)

Immediate steps for SEV-1 (high-impact degradation):
1) Pager to runtime-oncall and kernel-owner (see ownership table below).
2) Run: curl -sS http://fidelity-orchestrator.prod/_health | jq .; check last_reloaded_policy and decision_latency_ms.
3) If decision latency is high: switch router to bypass-orchestrator mode (router flag: --bypass-fidelity). This will pick safe defaults and fall back to serving runtime local heuristics. See section "Bypass mode".
4) If excessive degradation is due to policy change (identified by last_reloaded_policy matching recent commit), rollback policy via policy-store: git revert <policy-commit> and POST /v1/policies/reload.
5) If telemetry missing/stale: restart telemetry-ingest service and inspect ingestion lag (kafka consumer offset). Command: kubectl -n observability logs deploy/telemetry-ingest -c consumer | tail -n 200.
6) Post-incident: create an incident report with traces (decision_id list), affected tenants, and action items.

Bypass mode (safe default, fallthrough)
--------------------------------------
- Behavior: router skips orchestrator and uses serving-runtime heuristics:
  - default_kernel: kernel-lowlatency-safe-v1
  - exec_fidelity: balanced
  - quota_enforcement: unchanged
- Safe rollout: bypass is temporary and logged with reason. Router automatically re-enables orchestrator if decision API healthy for 3 consecutive 10s windows.

OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS
--------------------
- Fidelity Orchestrator service owner: runtime-control-plane (team alias)
- Primary oncall rotation: runtime-sre
- Kernel owner (low-latency kernels): kernel-scheduling team
- Observability: telemetry-platform

CONFIG TABLE (key, default, description)
---------------------------------------
| key | default | description |
| decision_api_timeout_ms | 25 | gRPC client timeout for router -> orchestrator |
| decision_cache_ttl_s | 30 | TTL for local decision cache |
| interactive_p99_target_ms | 150 | interactive p99 latency SLO |
| kvcache_cached_variant_cutoff | 0.6 | min kvcache_hit_ratio to prefer cached path |
| policy_canary_pct | 5 | percent traffic to canary during policy rollout |

ROLLOUT & CHANGE MANAGEMENT
---------------------------
- Policy changes must be checked into policy-store with a PR and two approvers: one from kernel-scheduling and one from runtime-sre.
- Canary rollout: set policy_canary_pct and gradually increase per the automated canary job. Metric gates:
  - no increase in tenant_error_rate > 0.1%
  - decision_api_p99_latency within 10% of baseline
  - degradation_rate < configured baseline + 2%
- Full promotion requires a successful 1h canary with gates passing and manual approval.

BENCHMARK & TESTING PLAN
------------------------
- Unit: mock telemetry harness with synthetic latency and kvcache hit injections.
- Integration: replay of production request signatures in the sandbox using the request-surface-replay tool (see related pages).
- Load test: run mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite against policy variations to measure decision_api_p99 and downstream kernel tail behavior.

SAMPLE POLICY (YAML snippet)
---------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: OrchestratorPolicy
metadata:
  id: interactive-default/v1
  author: marin.patel@redwood.ai
spec:
  match:
    interactive: true
  gates:
    - telemetry.kernel_latency_p99 < 150
    - telemetry.node_gpu_mem_free_mb > 800
  action:
    kernel_hint: kernel-lowlatency-v2
    exec_fidelity: balanced

DEBUGGING CHECKLIST
-------------------
1) Inspect decision trace for the request_id: curl "http://tracing.prod/decisions/{decision_id}".
2) Check telemetry snapshot age attached to the decision. If > 10s, prioritize fixing telemetry-ingest.
3) Validate policy against schema: ./tools/policy-validate policy.json
4) Reproduce locally using the sandbox replay tool: ./bin/replay --policy interactive-default/v1 --sample 1000

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS
---------------------
- Create a corrective PR for missing metric instrumentation.
- Add a unit test to policy CI for any edge-case that caused oscillation.
- Adjust canary gates to include the newly-observed signal if missing.

APPENDIX: EXAMPLE TRACE ANNOTATION (JSON)
----------------------------------------
{
  "decision_id": "uuid-xxxx",
  "policy_id": "policy/interactive-default/v1",
  "snapshot_age_ms": 4200,
  "telemetry_keys_used": ["kernel_latency_p99","kvcache_hit_ratio","node_gpu_mem_free_mb"],
  "score_explain": "selected lowlatency kernel: p99 120ms < 150ms and mem ok"
}
